title: IaC-driven SLO guardrails and canary workload for VPC upgrade automation
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Problem statement: Upgrades to Private (VPC) compute pools frequently rely on ad-hoc health checks and manual validation runs. This leads to inconsistent rollouts, late detection of regressions on latency/error-rate/saturation, and noisy on-call pages during upgrades.

Goal: Provide an IaC-first pattern (Terraform modules + upgrade pipeline hooks) that automatically provisions SLO measurement artifacts and runs gateable canary workloads during VPC/agent upgrades. The system should validate latency P95/P99, request error rates, GPU saturation markers, and token-window throughput before completing a rollout.

Design summary:
1) Implement a reusable Terraform module (slo_bootstrap_vpc) that provisions:
  - Prometheus recording rules for P50/P95/P99 latency and error-rate percentages (4xx/5xx)
  - Prometheus recording rules for per-pool GPU utilization and request queue depth
  - Recording rules for token-window metrics (tokens/sec, inflight-kv-entries)
  - Alerting rules that map to SLO burn-rate and short-term error spikes
  - Grafana dashboard provisioning for the above metrics with per-vpc template variables
  - A Kubernetes Job manifest template for canary load runs (k6/vegeta) and a ConfigMap for synthetic payloads

2) Upgrade pipeline integration:
  - Terraform apply invokes the slo_bootstrap_vpc module as part of the VPC module apply (idempotent)
  - Post-apply, run the canary Job against the new pool with a parameterized profile (ramp-up, steady-state, short-burst)
  - A short-run validator process collects recording rules and checks thresholds via Prometheus API; on failure it triggers the rollback path (terraform taint/rollback script)

3) Safety policies and thresholds (first pass):
  - Latency: P95 < 120ms, P99 < 350ms for light inference routes; for batching routes P95 < 250ms, P99 < 600ms
  - Errors: 5xx rate < 0.2% over 2m window, 4xx rate assessed per-route for client-side regressions
  - Saturation: GPU utilization < 92% sustained, request queue depth < 75% of configured queue watermark
  - Token throughput: sustained tokens/sec for the canary profile must be within ±15% of baseline traffic profile

4) Observability plumbing:
  - Use existing prometheus-cortex remote write and ensure slo_bootstrap_vpc writes per-vpc label scopes
  - Ensure dashboards and alert rules use tenancy labels (org_id, vpc_id, pool_id)

5) RBAC & safety:
  - SLO module creates read-only telemetry service account scoped to the pipeline for validation queries
  - Create a tfstate-locking contract for upgrade runs to avoid concurrent upgrades

Acceptance criteria:
- A terraform module lives in infra/terraform/modules/slo_bootstrap_vpc and can be consumed by private/vpc module
- Running the upgrade pipeline against a staging VPC automatically:
  1) provisions rules/dashboards, 2) runs the canary job, 3) validates SLOs, and 4) either marks the upgrade successful or triggers the documented rollback playbook
- Playbook exists in Confluence and is linked in the pipeline logs
- On-call pages for upgrades are reduced in noise for staged rollouts (target: 60% fewer pages during upgrade windows)
- Module is idempotent and covered by unit tests for Terraform plan diffs and integration smoke tests

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We use Prometheus recording rules instead of relying solely on raw queries to ensure cheap long-term evaluation and stable slos. The recording rules will be namespaced per-vpc to avoid cross-tenant mixing.
- Synthetic canaries will be lightweight (1–3 minute bursts) to reduce cost; for heavy workloads we add a 'stress' profile guarded behind a feature flag.
- Rollback automation will be conservative: on failure the pipeline pauses and notifies SRE with an optioned rollback; automated destroy should not be the default unless burnout conditions are met.
- We will prefer reusing the telemetry ingestion pipeline (Cortex) to avoid duplicating exporters.

On-call playbook excerpt: "If post-upgrade validation fails, the pipeline will: 1) tag the upgrade as FAILED, 2) create an incident with SRE runbook link, 3) pause further rollouts, and 4) optionally run rollback after SRE approval. Triage checklist: check recording rule cardinality, confirm remote-write ingestion, review canary job logs, and compare token-rate to baseline dashboard."

Notes for reviewers: "Focus reviews on: idempotency of Terraform module, security of created service accounts, and accuracy of recording rules (use correct histogram buckets for latency). Benchmarking guidance is in the Confluence doc (links above)."
